title: A food allergy is an abnormal immune reaction, and NIAID cites US rates near 8 and 11 percent
summary: NIAID says food allergy affects about 8 percent of US children and nearly 11 percent of US adults, and can be severe.
body: NIAID, the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, says it is the lead National Institutes of Health institute for food-allergy research. Its food-allergy page says the condition affects approximately 8 percent of children and nearly 11 percent of adults in the United States. In a person with food allergy, the immune system reacts abnormally to a component of a food, sometimes producing a severe and life-threatening response. Those percentages are the page's United States figures. They are not a world rate. This card does not describe how to treat a reaction. Emergency care for a severe allergic reaction is a different card.

sources.note: Supports the prevalence sentence and the immune-reaction sentence. The page did not show a reviewed date, so the source date is the access date. Public-domain NIH page. Paraphrased. No treatment steps.
